record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Interacting decaying Polya urns with forcing input
record.original_question: For a network of N >= 2 interacting reinforced stochastic processes with two actions S={0,1}, weighted adjacency matrix A, and dynamics Z_{n+1}=(1-r_r-r_f)Z_n+r_r X_{n+1}+r_f p with conditional mean E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=A^T Z_n, where r_f represents a forcing input toward p and r_r represents reinforcement, determine whether the discrete-time process Z_n fails to converge and whether it can be rescaled to a well-defined continuous-time interacting Wright-Fisher-type limit when r_f is asymptotic to c r_r^2. If such a limit exists, give a mathematically meaningful formulation of its dynamics and asymptotic behavior.

evidence.quote: It is also very interesting to understand whether or not the discrete-time process (Zn)n could be rescaled in order to get a proper time-continuous limiting process (Yt)t.
although the meaning of this dynamics and the asymptotic properties of this time-rescaled process are unknown at the moment.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 2$ and consider a network of $N$ agents, each choosing at every discrete time $n\in\mathbb{N}$ one of two actions in $S=\{0,1\}$. Let $A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ be a (row-stochastic) weighted adjacency matrix encoding the interaction. For each agent $i$, let $Z_n^{(i)}\in[0,1]$ be its "personal inclination" toward action $1$ at time $n$, and let $X_{n+1}^{(i)}\in\{0,1\}$ be its action at time $n+1$. Fix two sequences of reinforcement parameters $r_r=r_r(n)\in(0,1)$ and $r_f=r_f(n)\in(0,1)$ with $r_r+r_f<1$, and a fixed probability vector $p\in[0,1]^N$ (the forcing target). The joint dynamics is
$$Z_{n+1} \;=\; (1-r_r-r_f)\,Z_n \;+\; r_r\,X_{n+1} \;+\; r_f\,p,$$
where, conditionally on the natural filtration $\mathcal F_n$ generated by $(Z_0,X_1,\dots,X_n)$, the components $X_{n+1}^{(i)}$ are independent Bernoulli random variables with
$$\mathbb{E}[X_{n+1}\mid \mathcal F_n] \;=\; A^{\top} Z_n.$$
Here $r_r$ represents a (decaying) reinforcement strength and $r_f$ a forcing input pushing each $Z_n^{(i)}$ toward $p_i$.

Assume the asymptotic regime $r_f(n)\sim c\,r_r(n)^2$ as $n\to\infty$, for some constant $c>0$, with $r_r(n)\downarrow 0$.

(a) Prove or disprove that the discrete-time process $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$ fails to converge almost surely (and in distribution) as $n\to\infty$.

(b) Determine whether $(Z_n)_n$ admits a time rescaling $Y_t:=Z_{\lfloor t/r_r(n)\rfloor}$ (or some other natural rescaling depending on $r_r$, $r_f$) under which it converges, as $n\to\infty$, to a non-degenerate continuous-time Markov diffusion $(Y_t)_{t\ge 0}$ on $[0,1]^N$ of interacting Wright–Fisher type with mutation/drift coefficients depending on $A$, $p$ and $c$. If such a limit exists, give an explicit SDE characterization of its dynamics, identify its invariant measure, and describe its long-time asymptotic behavior.
artifact.status_search_result: The single-urn case (no network interaction) was treated by Aletti and Crimaldi (2021), where the rescaled Pólya urn with forcing scaled like $c r_r^2$ converges to a Wright–Fisher diffusion with mutation. For the interacting/network version with adjacency matrix $A$, no published result establishing the continuous-time interacting Wright–Fisher-type limit or characterizing its asymptotic behavior was located; recent works on reinforced stochastic processes on networks (e.g., 2025 hierarchical-network paper) do not address this scaling regime. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Rescaled Pólya Urn and the Wright–Fisher Process with Mutation
status_evidence.snippet: The multidimensional Wright-Fisher diffusion with mutation can be obtained as a suitable limit of the predictive means associated to a family of rescaled Pólya urns.
status_evidence.claim: Single-urn rescaled Pólya urn limit to Wright–Fisher established, but the network-interacting extension is not covered.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics for Reinforced Stochastic Processes on Hierarchical Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies asymptotics of reinforced stochastic processes on hierarchical networks but does not derive an interacting Wright–Fisher-type continuous-time limit in the r_f ~ c r_r^2 regime.
status_evidence.claim: Recent network-reinforced work does not resolve the interacting Wright–Fisher limit question.
